description: Stored exposure is a day count (ratio stored/date-derived clusters at 365) on 114 training rows (47 motor, 33 buildings, 34 contents). Convention established first from full-year rows: inclusive day count (end - start + 1) / 365, rounded to 4 dp; every test row obeys it exactly.
action_detail: exposure recomputed from period dates as (period_end - period_start + 1)/365 rounded to 4 dp for every row of every policy and test table; the test tables showed zero mismatches so their values are unchanged. Stored exposure sums fall from 54,429/33,783/38,893 to 38,969/23,468/29,058 exposure-years (motor/buildings/contents).
rationale: A 365x exposure on a few rows inflates line exposure by ~40% and would depress every burning cost and offset; the dates are internally consistent (no end before start) so they are the reliable source.

description: Stored exposure on a 360-day basis (ratio stored/date-derived clusters at 365/360 = 1.0139) on 493 training rows (206 motor, 121 buildings, 166 contents), found on the residual after the day-count cluster was removed; includes one 360-day row carrying exposure 1.0. None in test.
action_detail: same recomputation from dates as F-01 (applied to all rows, train and test). The ratio window was widened to 1.005-1.03 to catch short rows where 4-dp rounding blurs the 1.0139 ratio.
rationale: A second, smaller cluster hidden behind the day-count cluster (R-0014); 1.4% over-statement per row is immaterial individually but systematic.

description: Policy terms are 365 days, so in the leap year 2024 a full-year row runs 1 Jan - 30 Dec and no 2024 row ends on 31 Dec (2023: 93-96% of rows end 31 Dec; 2024: 0%). 2025 test rows ending 31 Dec are 365 days again. Not a defect, but any 'full year = ends Dec 31' logic would misclassify every 2024 row.
action_detail: Documented; exposure uses the 365-day convention consistently (a 2024 full-year row has exposure 1.0 and 365 days).
rationale: Reader warning for the profile and for completion calculations (loss ages are computed from actual dates, not from calendar years).

description: sum_insured recorded x1000 on 53 training and 104 test buildings rows (values up to 470,000,000 / 568,000,000). Decided per row on log10(written_premium / sum_insured): the cluster sits 3.00 decades below the main mass with an empty interval from -4.959 to -3.346 (train) and -4.973 to -3.312 (test); boundary placed at its midpoint (-4.152 / -4.142).
action_detail: sum_insured divided by 1000 on the rows below the boundary in both files; maximum after repair 813,000 (train) / 894,000 (test), inside the normal range. Year-on-year sum-insured ratios within a policy confirm the same rows (ratios >100 or <0.01).
rationale: A proportionality ratio separates a unit error from a genuinely large property (R-0013); a feature on the wrong scale in test rows would corrupt those predictions directly (R-0003).

description: sum_insured recorded x1000 on 57 training and 135 test contents rows (values up to 131,600,000 / 98,100,000). Decided per row on log10(written_premium / sum_insured): the cluster sits 3.02 decades below the main mass with an empty interval from -5.158 to -2.794 (train) and -5.187 to -2.783 (test); boundary placed at its midpoint (-3.976 / -3.985).
action_detail: sum_insured divided by 1000 on the rows below the boundary in both files; maximum after repair 235,000 (train) / 283,200 (test), inside the normal range. Year-on-year sum-insured ratios within a policy confirm the same rows (ratios >100 or <0.01).
rationale: A proportionality ratio separates a unit error from a genuinely large property (R-0013); a feature on the wrong scale in test rows would corrupt those predictions directly (R-0003).

description: 36 claims (92,267.26 CU net, 0.33% of incurred) have a loss_date before the first policy row of their policy (loss years 2021-2022, two in early 2023) and so link to no row. Their report lags are 411-565 days, all beyond the matched claims' 99.5% lag (334 d) and 11 beyond the 99.9% (505 d): a date defect, not late reporting. All 36 policies exist in the policy tables; no claim fell in a gap between rows or after the last row.
action_detail: Removed from cleaned/claims.parquet; not re-dated. Share of incurred stated so the level effect is bounded (0.33%).
rationale: R-0015: lags beyond the matched extreme quantile mark a date defect; re-dating would invent a loss date. A human should confirm whether these belong to pre-2023 policy years outside the extract or carry mis-keyed years.

description: Content-key duplicate test on (policy_id, peril, loss_date, paid, incurred, recoveries) and the looser keys (policy, peril, loss_date) and (policy, loss_date, incurred): no duplicates found. Four pairs share (policy, loss_date) with different perils (own damage + third-party property / bodily injury from one accident) and are legitimate multi-peril events.
action_detail: Negative result recorded; dedup step kept in the pipeline (removes zero rows).
rationale: R-0002 requires the check to be run and its negative result kept in the audit trail.

description: Claims internal checks passed: paid <= incurred (0 violations), recoveries <= incurred (0), report_date >= loss_date (0), nothing after the 2024-12-31 valuation (0; latest loss 2024-12-29, latest report 2024-12-30), no negative amounts, closed claims have paid == incurred, no claim in the 2025 test period. 120 repudiated claims carry zero amounts and contribute zero to the target.
action_detail: Repudiated claims kept in the cleaned table with their status; target construction sets them to zero (R-0101).
rationale: Valuation-date and future-information check (R-0007) and target definition (R-0101).

description: December 2024 (the last month before valuation) has 268 claims against 330-420 in other 2024 months, with the shortfall concentrated in the long-lag perils (third-party property 42 vs ~90-105/month, bodily injury 1 vs ~20): systematic under-reporting of the last calendar month. 2024 open-claim share is 20-25% against 0-4% for 2023.
action_detail: Carried by the completion curve in target construction (row completion 0.83 for 2024 motor rows), not by an ad-hoc fix.
rationale: R-0106: the completion curve, not a manual adjustment, must carry late reporting; mentioned wherever months are compared.

description: Dominant large losses: buildings fire claims of 125k-361k CU each exceed 2-10% of their accident year's buildings total (one 2024 fire = 9.7% of 2024 buildings incurred); 2024 motor has one open bodily-injury claim of 156k (2% of the year). Top 1% of claims carry 16% (motor), 26% (buildings), 13% (contents) of net incurred.
action_detail: Not deleted. Handed to target construction: row targets capped at the 99th percentile of positive rows per line (motor 21,148, buildings 143,434, contents 19,968 CU) with the excess returned as a line multiplier (1.0775 / 1.1188 / 1.0526); lag curves weight claims capped at their 99th percentile.
rationale: R-0008: one such claim distorts trend, development and segment comparisons; buildings comparisons between years and markets are made on a capped basis (R-0411).

description: customer_since_year is a deterministic function of the customer's first policy year: every customer first seen in 2025 (test only) has customer_since_year 2025, every 2024 joiner 2024, and all earlier values occur only among 2023 customers. Single-feature adversarial AUC (2024 train vs 2025 test) 0.88.
action_detail: Column retained in cleaned tables; in the modelling tables it is renamed x_customer_since_year and excluded from the feature set. The relative quantity tenure_years = policy year - customer_since_year is derived instead (identical meaning in training and test).
rationale: R-0016/R-0006: a join-year identifier is a time stamp, not a risk factor; it would price the whole acquired book as 'unseen cohort'.

description: campaign_code is null for exactly the customers with customer_since_year <= 2022 (100% null) and populated for every 2023-2025 joiner (0% null): the nullness encodes 'joined before the campaign system existed'. Adversarial AUC of the null indicator 0.79. The 15 populated codes are uniformly distributed and carry no claim signal.
action_detail: Retained in cleaned tables; renamed x_campaign_code in the modelling tables and excluded from features.
rationale: R-0016: an attribute null exactly for customers who joined before a system existed is a cohort stamp.

description: customer_service_contacts grows mechanically with the claims in the same row: rows with 0 contacts have 0 claims, 1 contact 0.04 claims/yr, 2 contacts 0.25, 4+ contacts 1.18 (motor); its upper tail exists only in training (max 20/11/11 vs 5/6/5 in test; mean 0.81 vs 0.40 motor). Prior-year contacts predict next-year frequency only through prior claims.
action_detail: Retained in cleaned tables; renamed x_customer_service_contacts in the modelling tables and excluded from features. renewal_decision (end-of-period outcome, absent from test) is likewise carried as x_renewal_decision.
rationale: R-0005: a count recorded during the period whose value grows with the claims it is meant to predict is not available at pricing time in the same form.

description: missed_payments_12m tested under R-0005 and kept: its distribution is identical in training and test (mean 0.10, p99 = 2, max 5-7 in both), and the prior-year value predicts next-year frequency as strongly as the same-year value (2024 frequency 0.094 / 0.123 / 0.118 by 2023 count 0/1/2+ vs 0.093 / 0.130 / 0.132 by 2024 count), so the signal is customer financial stress, not in-period claim handling.
action_detail: Kept as a feature; negative result recorded.
rationale: R-0005 requires each behavioural count to be tested, not excluded by name.

description: The weather table carries 2025 (prediction-year) values for every address. 2025 differs from 2024 at every address and the yearly means move (freezing days 17.5 -> 28.9, rainfall 1375 -> 1251 mm, hail days 17.1 -> 11.4); each index alone separates 2024 from 2025 rows with AUC 0.55-0.75. Year-to-year correlation at an address is 0.2 (hail) to 0.94 (rainfall), so the yearly value is mostly a year effect for the volatile indices.
action_detail: Weather table copied through unchanged. Yearly weather values are excluded from features; the modelling tables carry an optional address-level mean over the training years only (wx_*_mean2324), flagged as an optional group to be tested, not in the lean baseline (Part 1 found weather hurt out-of-year performance).
rationale: R-0022: prediction-year environmental data that could not be known when the policies were priced is a calendar stamp by default.

description: occupation has 81 distinct raw values against a 20-value code list (the developed market's): case variants ('retired', 'Retired'), trailing whitespace ('Nurse '), and a 'Self-employed ' prefix attached at a uniform ~10% rate to every base occupation including 'retired', 'student' and 'unemployed' where it is meaningless. Uniform rate = random corruption (R-0021), not a real attribute.
action_detail: Lower-cased, whitespace-stripped, 'self-employed ' prefix removed, first letter capitalised to match the developed code list: 81 -> 20 levels plus null; 59899 customers relabelled (11975 prefix, 47924 case/whitespace only). Customers table is shared by training and test rows.
rationale: Spurious levels split thin categories and would differ between the two markets' encodings; the uniform-rate test shows the prefix carries no information.

description: Fourteen columns are null on ~12% of rows each (customers: occupation, marital_status, household_size, years_at_address; addresses: distance_to_river_km, soil_type, roof_type, energy_rating; motor: vehicle_age, engine_size_cc, overnight_parking; buildings: days_unoccupied, smoke_alarms; contents: security_level, high_value_items), identical in training and test and across join cohorts. Nulls are independent draws: co-missingness equals the marginal rate, null rows match non-null rows on every other covariate (standardised differences < 0.04), claim frequency and burning cost do not differ by nullness, and for policy attributes the null falls on one row of a multi-row policy at the rate expected by chance (the developed market has 2.5% nulls on the same columns).
action_detail: No mode imputation and no indicator features (R-0018: independent draws). Nulls kept as missing (the tree learner handles them natively); entity-level nulls in customers/addresses cannot be reconstructed. Policy-stable attributes are reconstructed from sibling rows (F-18).
rationale: R-0018: test for MAR before choosing a treatment; indicator features for MCAR nulls add noise.

description: Nullable policy attributes that are constant within a policy across its rows (overnight_parking, security_level, high_value_items: 100% of multi-row policies carry a single value; smoke_alarms 95%; engine_size_cc and vehicle_age are constant/incrementing within policy and make_model) can be reconstructed from a sibling row of the same policy. days_unoccupied is a per-period quantity (3% constant) and is not reconstructed.
action_detail: Null filled from the latest non-null sibling row of the same policy (train and test rows pooled, since the attribute is time-invariant); engine_size_cc only from a sibling with the same make_model, vehicle_age from such a sibling plus the year difference. motor.overnight_parking: train 5697->173, test 10859->7219; motor.engine_size_cc: train 5745->538, test 11004->8660; motor.vehicle_age: train 5604->529, test 11070->8694; buildings.smoke_alarms: train 3266->149, test 6341->4554; contents.security_level: train 4238->158, test 8050->5629; contents.high_value_items: train 4067->115, test 7954->5553. New-business test rows have no sibling and keep their nulls. Modelling tables flag filled rows as dq_<column>_sibling_filled.
rationale: Closest-to-truth repair for an attribute that provably does not change; reduces training nulls on these columns from 12% to about 1% and test nulls to the new-business share.

description: flood_zone nulls (2.9% of addresses) are not at random: null addresses sit closer to rivers (median distance 1.15 km vs 2.40 km) and lower (elevation 7.4 m vs 9.8 m), and buildings rows at null-flood-zone addresses show frequency 0.065 vs 0.044 and burning cost 833 vs 395 CU (43 claims, thin). Same pattern and rate in the developed market.
action_detail: Kept as its own 'unknown' level (null retained; no imputation to the mode 1.0).
rationale: R-0018: a null group that differs systematically carries risk information and must not be imputed away.

description: 2023 is a survivor sample: 100% of 2023 policies appear in 2024 in all three lines, and 2023 has no 'cancelled' or 'lapsed_by_customer' rows at all (2024 has 3,619 / 2,191 / 2,764 such rows and 85% persistence into 2025). The extract reaches back only for policies still in force in 2024, so 2023 frequency and mix are conditioned on survival.
action_detail: Rows kept; flagged dq_survivor_year in the modelling tables; labelled in the shift report and validation design (the 2023-only training fold predicts a non-survivor 2024).
rationale: R-0020: a year with complete persistence and no lapses must be labelled as a survivor sample.

description: renewal_decision = 'declined_by_insurer' does not end the policy: 100% of 2023 declined policies have a 2024 row and 75-95% of 2024 declined policies have a 2025 test row, whereas 'cancelled' and 'lapsed_by_customer' show 0% persistence. 91% of declined rows carry a claim (vs 7% otherwise) and they average 3-4 service contacts, so the value marks a claim outcome rather than a renewal decision.
action_detail: Rows kept; renewal_decision is post-period information (absent from test) and is not a feature in any case.
rationale: R-0020: a value that should end a policy but shows near-complete persistence is a semantic defect to query, not a risk segment.

description: expenses.emerging is null for commission_comparison_site although 2,316 training and 4,530 test motor rows (plus 1,410/2,624 buildings and 1,745/3,304 contents) are written through the comparison_site channel. Every other expense item is populated; the emerging loadings differ materially from the developed ones (fixed expense 85 vs 45 CU, broker commission 20% vs 15%, premium tax 8% vs 12%, cat reinsurance 12% vs 6%).
action_detail: Table copied through unchanged; not filled in. Premium build must not proceed for the comparison_site channel until the loading is confirmed.
rationale: R-0412: a missing entry in a loading table is a premium-build question, never something to fill silently.

description: reference_policies holds 20 rows (7 motor, 7 buildings, 6 contents) that are exact copies of 2025 test rows (same row_id, policy_id, customer and address) stacked into one wide schema with a 'line' column, other lines' columns null, and numeric types widened to float (years_licensed, ncb_years, seats). 18 of 20 are new business. Its purpose (reference quotes for a rate check? sample for the premium build?) is not documented.
action_detail: Copied through unchanged; not used in modelling (the rows are already in the test files with their original types).
rationale: A table whose role is unstated should not be silently used or dropped; the team should say what it is for.

description: compulsory_excess takes a single value per line (250 CU motor, 350 CU buildings and contents) in training and test, so it carries no information; the developed market has the same constants.
action_detail: Kept in cleaned tables; dropped from the feature list.
rationale: Constant columns cannot be learned from and clutter the feature audit.

description: Open-claim adequacy (IBNER) view: open claims are a selected sample (2024 motor open mean 4,088 CU vs closed 1,724; 2023 open 11,164 vs closed 1,958; buildings 2024 open 9,463 vs closed 6,043). The older year's open claims at the same age are not observable in a two-year extract, so no like-for-like comparison is possible and no uplift is applied; recorded as an uncertainty in target_notes.
action_detail: Open claims taken at case estimate (R-0101); IBNER uplift not adopted (R-0105).
rationale: R-0105: do not adopt an IBNER view blind; validation years carry the same reserving bias.
